title: Fix the Bug: Voting Age Boundary
hints: Check the boundary: can an 18-year-old vote?
jsBridge: The same lesson in every language: `cond ? true : false` is just `cond`. The Swift angle: `Bool` is its own type, so there's no `!!value` coercion trick and no truthiness to fall back on.

compass.q: JS uses `!!x` to coerce to boolean. Why does Swift not need, or allow, that?
Age thresholds differ by country. Where should that rule live so it isn't hard-coded in a view?
Should age be `Int` or `UInt`? What would `UInt` change, and why does Swift style prefer `Int` anyway?
A computed property `var canVote: Bool` vs a function `canVote(age:)`: when is each the better API?
